summary: This rule explains who must follow a specific set of stock market duties. It applies only to companies that have listed certain non-convertible securities. It also clarifies how words like interest and default are understood.
points: Follow this chapter only if your non-convertible securities are listed on a recognized stock exchange.
List those securities according to the specified 2021 regulations.
Read the word interest as dividend if you have listed certain preference shares or similar instruments.
Treat any failure to pay interest, dividend, or principal in full on the pre-agreed date as a default.
Recognize a default immediately at the very first instance of delay.
example: Meera Textiles Private Limited listed its non-convertible redeemable preference shares on a recognized stock exchange following the 2021 regulations. Because of this, the company falls under the rules of this chapter. The company was supposed to pay a dividend to its investors on a pre-agreed date, but the payment was delayed by one day. Under the rules, this first instance of delay immediately counts as a default. Since these are preference shares, the rule treats what would normally be called interest as a dividend for all the requirements in this section of the law.

terms.meaning: Investments like bonds or preference shares that cannot be changed into equity shares.
Failing to pay money owed, such as interest, dividend, or principal, in full on the agreed date.
An official market approved for trading securities.

watch: Do not wait for a grace period because a default is recognized at the very first instance of delay.
